An elbow-length-sleeved straight-cut cotton T-shirt, a real plain T-shirt and not a real garment, covered edge to edge in a lifelike photographic full-coverage print with natural fabric texture and shading, designed to make the shirt look like the outfit of a teacher. The design is enlarged to fill the entire shirt, edge to edge, with no blank margin around it. The printed outfit runs from the neckline to the hem and from one sleeve hem to the other, its shoulders on the shirt's shoulder seams, showing a tweed jacket with chalk-dusted elbow patches. The print wraps all the way round, the back of the shirt shows the rear of the outfit from the back collar to the hem and along both sleeves. The outfit's fabric runs seamlessly over the shoulders and down the sleeves, every part of the shirt in the outfit's own colours and textures. The shirt keeps the outline of an ordinary T-shirt, round neckline, straight side seams, sleeves, and a straight open hem. The printed top garment continues down the shirt to its straight hem, with at most a belt or sash at the waist. The print is cut exactly to the shirt, neck, shoulders, armholes, sleeves and hem are all covered in the outfit's own fabric. The outfit is stretched to the shirt's own straight-sided shape and fills it completely, so it suits any body size. The shirt's sleeves are tailored to end at the elbow, exactly where the outfit's sleeves end. All textures, transparencies and sheens are printed patterns on solid cotton. The picture is only the garment, its cloth, seams, buttons and trims laid flat across the whole shirt like a sewing pattern. It also shows printed cuffs and wrists at the sleeve hems. The illusion is purely flat and two-dimensional, with no real fabric, buttons or pockets beyond the print. To read as a costume rather than a plain top, it adds the outfit's patches, insignia and emblems, the held item or gear of the outfit, shown as a patch or large motif on the chest or a sleeve and the collar, neckwear and fastenings of the outfit, bold and large enough to identify the outfit from across a room. Any printed skin, such as hands, wrists, neck, chest or forearms, is in a flat printed golden olive skin tone.

The outfit is printed across the whole front, over the shoulders and down both sleeves, showing a polka-dot jumpsuit with a huge bow tie. Front and back are both fully printed, the back showing how the same outfit looks from behind. The outfit's fabric runs seamlessly over the shoulders and down the sleeves, every part of the shirt in the outfit's own colours and textures. It is an ordinary T-shirt in shape, with a straight open hem and sleeves cut to match the outfit's sleeves. The printed top garment continues down the shirt to its straight hem, with at most a belt or sash at the waist. The print is cut exactly to the shirt, neck, shoulders, armholes, sleeves and hem are all covered in the outfit's own fabric. The uniform fills the whole straight-sided shirt shape edge to edge, the same width at chest, waist and hem. The shirt is a long-sleeved T-shirt matching the outfit's long sleeves, printed with the sleeves and cuffs all the way down to the wrist hems. The shirt is solid opaque cotton and every texture and sheen is a printed picture. Only the outfit's fabric, trims and fastenings are pictured, spread across the entire shirt as a continuous pattern. It also shows printed cuffs where the sleeves end. It is a trompe-l'oeil T-shirt, a plain cotton shirt pretending to be the outfit. It carries enough of the costume to be unmistakable, the lower garment's colours and pattern as a band across the hem, the most recognisable props and accessories of the outfit as appliqué pieces and the held item or gear of the outfit, shown as a patch or large motif on the chest or a sleeve, all in the outfit's own colours. Any printed skin, such as hands, wrists, neck, chest or forearms, is in a flat printed golden olive skin tone.
